extracted.intended_audience: Reuters reporters, editors and newsroom staff (desk editors, correspondents, bureaux)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical newsroom style and production rules for composing, tagging, slugging, scheduling and filing stories on the Reuters wire, covering story types (spot, sidebar, curtainraiser, instant view, highlights, interview, pools, etc.) and operational metadata (slugs, USNs, skedlines, sign-offs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline tag: single tag only
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines carry only a single tag to avoid a confusing clutter of tags on screens (so just UPDATE X or ANALYSIS or EXCLUSIVE for instance, but not UPDATE X-ANALYSIS-).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tag to use is down to the judgment of the regional editing desk. Exception: if you correct or refile a tagged story, there would be two tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: EXCLUSIVE tag usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The EXCLUSIVE tag is for our very top exclusives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Its use should only be approved by news editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: INSIGHT piece definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An INSIGHT piece should reveal something that our readers didn't know, and should have original reporting in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should not be a roundup of news combined with a survey of experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANALYSIS piece definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANALYSIS piece can take a quick-hit analytical view of a subject and can rely more on experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It must be based on reportage and not simply on the author's own ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool reports: definition and ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A pool is a limited group of journalists from different news services who report on behalf of the entire press corps when space is limited or there are other constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground rules and selection procedures should be clearly defined and understood by participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool story formats (three kinds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three basic kinds of pools: (1) a single story is written on behalf of all pool members; (2) individual pool members write their own stories filed on a collective pool basis; (3) the pool writer provides a detailed chronological account in note form and journalists write their own stories from that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool byline/advisory when Reuters wrote the story
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Reuters member of the pool has written the story we should use his or her byline and an advisory line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example advisory: (This story was written by Reuters correspondent Jane Smith on behalf of the pool of White House correspondents in Saudi Arabia.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool advisory when Reuters did not write the story
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Reuters correspondent did not write the story we should not use a byline and should file an advisory line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example advisory: (The pool of White House correspondents in Saudi Arabia of which Jane Smith of Reuters is a member wrote this story.) Add the word (POOL) to the slug of a pooled story, e.g. BC-TRANSMENIA-HOSTAGES (POOL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule purpose and principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schedule (Sked) is primarily a planning tool for media clients, providing a present-tense approximation of first paragraphs of major stories planned or moving; it also serves as a news planning tool for editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News must never be 'saved for the Sked' — publish news as it happens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule issue times and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: World News Schedules and Business News Schedules are issued multiple times daily (World News six times; World Business three times; regional variations apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional/desk-specific schedule issue times must be followed (specific GMT/NY times listed in operations). Wires go only to media clients so RICs should not be used on business schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skedline content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A skedline must state whether there is a picture or television images, at what time the story moved or is expected to move, and how many words the story has or is expected to run to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should be no 'cycle identifier' preceding the slug. Style times appropriately (e.g. 0900 GMT or 9 a.m. EST/EDT). Example skedline format provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skedline submission timing and coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Skedlines should be sent at least half an hour before the Schedule is issued and coded appropriately for region/desk (e.g. SKEDLINE in Cy-Slug or NEXT plus desk code for other regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add reasonable time for desk editing; advise the desk if you are unable to meet the landing time; on big breaking stories send after Newsbreak; send holding skedlines if important event is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign-offs: structure and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign-offs give contact details for people most involved in researching and editing a story, demonstrating accountability and giving clients a contact point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign-off comprises a first line in single parentheses listing main people (e.g. Reporting by; Editing by) and a second section in double parentheses giving contact information for the reporter. Single-parentheses info goes to all clients; double-parentheses contact info is stripped for media clients and only goes to financial clients. Format and capitalization rules specified; separate items with semi-colons; include telephone in +country format; do not add extraneous names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylined story sign-off rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A story that carries a byline does not carry a 'Reporting by' entry to avoid duplication of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign-off example: (Editing by June Singh)((sam.thomas@reuters.com; +1 646 897 1898; Reuters Messaging: sam.thomas.reuters.com@reuters.net)). For double bylined stories add both contact sets on merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylined story with additional reporters credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Other reporters who contributed to a bylined story are credited with 'Additional reporting by' and locations if different from the dateline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (Additional reporting by Mohan Kumar in Bangkok; Editing by June Singh)((...)). 'Additional reporting by' not warranted for minimal contributions like a 'no comment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: No byline story sign-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories with no byline carry a single 'Reporting by' credit that lists one or more reporters that worked on the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sign-off: (Reporting by Sam Thomas and Mohan Kumar; Editing by June Singh)((...)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing by field rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Editing by' field should usually show the name of the last person who edited the story or the person who did the most substantial edit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If edited in the bureau before being sent to the desk, show both the bureau editor and the person who finally pushed the button. Never show more than two names in this field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing by usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Writing by' is used on stories where the on-the-spot reporter can report but not write, or where a journalist has written a story drawing substantially on a series of stories from another Reuters service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details in double parentheses should be for the writer; reason: reporter may not be easy to reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated by usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Translated by' used on stories translated into another language, alongside credits for original reporter(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details should be those of the translator unless the reporter can handle queries in the new language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive/dangerous circumstances rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If reporters cannot be named because identification could endanger them, leave the name off the story and use contact details for the desk or bureau Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stringers contact-rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reporter is a stringer who does not have Reuters contact details, use their name as reporter but use contact details for the bureau or editor which handled the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot use the stringer's name, use the editor's name and contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slug structure: packaging/wild/format
rubrics_metrics.description: A slug has three parts: the PACKAGING SLUG (before the /), the WILD SLUG (after the /) and STORY FORMAT information in parentheses at the end (e.g. (ANALYSIS, UPDATE 1, PIX, TV)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packaging slug pulls packages together and must stay the same for running stories; wild slug differentiates individual stories within a package; format shows story type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging slug rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Packaging slugs must stay consistent for as long as the story runs through updates and must be a minimum of two words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's more important that a packaging slug is consistent than perfect. Keep slug simple and unlikely to need changing. Use packaging slug for trunk updates and wrap-ups only; do not change to improve relevance on running stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wild slug rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The wild slug distinguishes a story from previous ones in the package and clients use it to split stories within a package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A trunk update or wrapup does NOT have a wild slug. No two stories published on the same day should carry an identical wild slug.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story format parentheses rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Story format information (ANALYSIS, UPDATE 1, PIX, TV etc.) goes in parentheses at the end of the slug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the packaging slug for trunk updates and wrap-ups; nothing goes after the / except story format info in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slugging tips and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan slugs in advance as part of news planning; consult regional editing desk which has final say; keep packaging slug likely to last through story life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure of previous slug, check Kobra/Eikon or Lynx Editor. If forced to change a slug on a trunk story, send an Advisory to media product codes and email online production desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slugging FAQs / practical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical answers: yes always include a forward slash; trunk stories carry packaging slug only; hyphens allowed after slash; avoid single-word country or company slugs; use target company name in mergers; avoid acronyms unless globally known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and rationales given (single-word slugs cause visual attachments to transfer; use COMPANYNAME-EARNINGS/ etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Story Number (USN) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The USN links together pages of a story on terminals; the same USN used on each page allows systems to join pages and permits corrections, overwrites and replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USNs must be enclosed by square brackets and preceded by an 'n' when used as a navigational tool in summaries (e.g. [nSYD12345]).

rubrics_metrics.name: USN drill (how USNs change through cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A snap and newsbreak carry the same USN. The UPDATE 1 to that newsbreak takes a new USN and all subsequent updates retain that USN through the rest of the 24-hour news cycle. When a story begins without a snap or newsbreak, the USN remains the same on all subsequent updates through the 24-hour cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to all types of story.

rubrics_metrics.name: USN exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to USN rules include corrected stories and market reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected story should take the same USN as the story it replaces; the next update should take a new USN which remains on subsequent updates. Market reports each take a separate USN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline length and slug mandatory rule
rubrics_metrics.description: ALL headlines on all types of stories should be no more than 64 characters including headline tags; all stories except Alerts must have a slug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Thomson Reuters products cannot handle longer headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take length / splitting long stories
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories (including Tables, Factboxes etc.) should be filed in one page (take) except in cases of extreme length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPS has a 10,000-character limit per document, translating to ~1500 words or 150-160 lines; above that a story must be split into multiple takes and reopened using exactly the same slug with =2, =3 appended to the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot story writing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Write spot news quickly, clearly and simply; say what happened and why we are reporting it, in language that is easy to translate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put news in context with quotes, colour and background; be precise with sourcing; adhere to Reuters core values of accuracy, speed and objectivity; do not update for the sake of it—only on merit. If updated, the first version should remain on screen; updates take new USNs as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sidebar rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sidebar is a spot story filed as a companion piece to a running 'trunk' story and should use the slug of the trunk story plus an additional identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format and writing same as basic spot story though context/background may be sketched. Tabular/bullet formats can work. Avoid updates if possible as they can cause confusion for screen readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curtainraiser / holding story rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Curtainraisers are written ahead of set-piece events and carry the PREVIEW tag and (PREVIEW) after the slug and PRE topic code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question the news value before writing. Stand a chance only if written in a newsworthy fashion. Standard curtainraiser: file 2-3 days before event, max 600 words (shorter is better), latest should be noon on the day before event; do not issue in daylight hours on the day of the event. Consult regional desk and link the event to context, likely outcome and quotable sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overnighter definition and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: An overnighter restarts a major ongoing story with a write-through for the next news cycle by adding a forward-looking element and should be reserved for stories likely to appear on a top news page or schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach as a bridge between two days and aim to throw the story forward or provide a fresh take; do not repeat stale facts; an overnighter takes its own USN; consult regional desk on necessity and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instant View: purpose and tag
rubrics_metrics.description: INSTANT VIEW (or ANALYSTS VIEW) provides rapid reaction from analysts/decision makers to significant spot breaking or diarised events and must carry the INSTANT VIEW headline tag and a slug (e.g. XXX/YYY (INSTANT VIEW)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are two types (analyst quotes compilation; one-stop shop data reaction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instant View type 1: analyst quotes rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: First type compiles direct quotes of no fewer than three analysts and should be updated as entries are added without the UPDATE tag; begin with a dateline and short note describing the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write name, title and organisation in upper case above each quote. The first entry on economic/financial news should reach screens within 15 minutes of the event and the series must be completed within 30 minutes. If obtained after 15 minutes use the tag ANALYSTS' VIEW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instant View type 2: one-stop shop and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Second type gives a one-stop shop for clients directly after data or a news event so customers need not flick between items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essence is speed; aim to land on big events within a 15-20 minute window while the market is paying attention. With general/political news, keep Instant View updated up to two hours then convert to a FACTBOX of best quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlights format: purpose and basic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: HIGHLIGHTS provide key quotes and facts during fast-moving events so clients can get consolidated info without scanning multiple small stories; use HIGHLIGHTS tag and slug with HIGHLIGHTS in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subheads to group ideas (e.g. RATES, INFLATION); add 'THIS ITEM WILL BE UPDATED' when appropriate; refresh frequently; set USN management and R message type as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlights production and XREF rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Production of Highlights is labour intensive—one person files snaps, another checks, a subeditor compiles, and ideally another files XREFs to snaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use XREFs to link snaps to the Highlights USN; file description text without a headline for XREFs; if changing an XREF already filed use 'O' not 'R' to avoid losing snaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlights length and USN management
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch length: 130 lines is the maximum for one take; change USN frequently in a long series to avoid repeating the whole sequence on a correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert new information at the top with 'LATEST QUOTES' then 'EARLIER QUOTES'; capitalise subheads and keep them short; clean up when event ends to prioritise most important info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking quotes: selection and paraphrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Be selective when taking quotes: focus on key quotes rather than complete transcript; paraphrase lengthy non-snap material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a speaker responds to a question include the question only if essential, and paraphrase it for brevity. Use short summaries like 'DOLLAR OVERVALUED?' as faster and more effective captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview tag usage and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: INTERVIEW tag and slug are for substantive interviews with subjects of note and should not be used for a few shouted questions in a scrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare well, advise photo/video teams, and write 'told Reuters' or 'said in an interview'. Outstanding interviews may use the EXCLUSIVE tag (subject to editorial approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: TEXT Q&A excerpts rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A TEXT of Q&A excerpts may be used after a major interview and must repeat all quotes (with questions) used in the main story and carry additional edited questions and answers written in order.
